# Verification analysis: alias-based-policy-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-05__12-23-47`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` routes between `lan-a` and `lan-b`. Permit `node2` to reach `node3`
> on TCP ports 8080, 8443 and 9000, expressing that set of ports as a single
> named object on `node1` and referring to the object from the rule instead of
> writing one rule for each port.

- Networks: **mgmt, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `alias-based-policy-rhel7__4kCMH6m`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The task's material outcomes are all satisfied with direct evidence: node1 was configured with opt1/opt2 interfaces and forwarding to route between lan-a and lan-b; a single named port alias (node3_svc_ports, containing 8080/8443/9000) was created on node1 and a single firewall rule on interface opt1 references that alias (rather than three separate per-port rules) to permit node2→node3 traffic; and TCP connectivity tests directly confirm the three listed ports are reachable while an unlisted port (9999) is blocked, both before and after each node's individual restart. The independent restart protocol was completed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3), and confirmed recovery of interfaces, routes, the alias/rule, firewalld rules, and end-to-end connectivity.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.900 | 61/13 (+6 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
  - **Why:** opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.254/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.254/24) added to node1 config.xml, applied via configctl interface reconfigure, IP forwarding confirmed enabled (net.inet.ip.forwarding=1). End-to-end TCP connectivity between node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b) verified through node1, both before and after node1's restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2b34003f8e2c406d`, `cmd-2d6ce1c5866d44f6`, `cmd-0946c75e23064eb2`, `cmd-16451c768bfd4303`, `cmd-29ce00fd35d4495e`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Port set 8080/8443/9000 expressed as a single named alias object on node1
  - **Why:** A port-type alias named node3_svc_ports containing 8080, 8443, 9000 was added to OPNsense/Firewall/Alias/aliases in config.xml, confirmed both in the XML tree and via pfctl -sr showing 'node3_svc_ports = "{ 8080 8443 9000 }"'.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cb02f3dda26944a7`, `cmd-1547ef5935aa40f2`, `cmd-9e480adaedf145cc`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** A single firewall rule refers to the alias instead of one rule per port
  - **Why:** Only one <rule> element was added to config.xml (interface opt1, source 10.60.1.11, destination 10.60.2.12, destination port set to the alias name node3_svc_ports). The compiled pf ruleset (pfctl -sr) shows this expanded into three port-specific pass lines, but all three share the identical rule label (a hash of the single source rule), confirming they originate from one config-level rule referencing one alias, not three manually authored rules.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d22166f27f584f8e`, `cmd-1c7ad73c68a9499a`, `cmd-9e480adaedf145cc`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, 9000 and is blocked on other ports (e.g. 9999)
  - **Why:** Before the firewalld rich rules were added on node3, all ports timed out/failed. After adding the alias-referencing pf rule on node1 and matching firewalld rich rules on node3 (scoped to node2's IP), TCP connections from node2 to node3 succeeded with banner responses on 8080/8443/9000 and timed out on 9999. Re-verified again after all three nodes were restarted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e7ef27596f2c44d5`, `cmd-cb5a7895d084497b`, `cmd-2590904b25634e32`, `cmd-4ddaac027f024fdd`, `cmd-e5d9cd46efcc4858`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state (provider-wide protocol)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart kern.boottime captured (17:06:27) along with intact opt1/opt2 addressing and pf rule. Reboot issued; SSH connection timeouts observed during the outage window; kern.boottime changed to 17:12:41 post-restart; opt1/opt2 addresses, the alias-referencing pf rule, and IP forwarding were all confirmed intact, and end-to-end connectivity to node3 was re-verified afterward.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Executor commands were largely read-only discovery or directly purposeful mutations (bringing up interfaces, editing config.xml, adding the alias/rule, adding routes, opening firewalld rich rules, running restart verification). A few minor items are worth noting: (1) node1's /conf/config.xml.bak1/.bak2/.bak3 backup copies were created before each XML edit and left in place — low-risk, standard safety practice, no functional impact. (2) The ad-hoc TCP test listener on node3 (python2 /tmp/listen.py and associated /tmp/nc*.log files) was left running and its files remain in /tmp after the executor finished (visible in the after-executor snapshot's listening-sockets and temporary-files diffs for node3); this is verification tooling rather than task-required state, and was not cleaned up, though it is low-risk (a python2 script bound to test ports, not exposed beyond the lab network) and did not conflict with or weaken the actual firewall/alias configuration delivered. (3) Several early attempts (nmcli without sudo, configctl interface reload variants, ip/ifconfig/python3 tool-discovery failures) failed with return codes 1/10/127 but made no state changes — these are appropriately treated as discovery, not hygiene issues. No damaged package state, no failed services, and no weakened security controls were observed in the before/after-executor comparison; firewalld and pf remained active and correctly scoped throughout.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-2b34003f8e2c406d`, `cmd-cb02f3dda26944a7`, `cmd-d22166f27f584f8e`, `cmd-75c8bc3ae3cf48b5`, `cmd-27aba510db694755`, `cmd-d153c5534ead4587`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets`

### Comments and limitations

- Package-manager health checks were unavailable/timed out on node2 and node3 throughout (before, after-prepare, and after-executor), so package-state integrity could not be independently verified via that channel.
- The compiled pf ruleset (pfctl -sr) displays the port-alias rule as three separate pass lines sharing one rule label rather than a single line with a bracketed port set; this is standard pf/OPNsense rule-compilation behavior for port aliases and the underlying config.xml confirms a single <rule> element and a single named alias, but a reviewer relying only on pfctl -sr output without the config.xml evidence could misread this as three separate rules.
- The ad-hoc TCP test listener and its log files left running on node3 after task completion are verification artifacts, not part of the delivered configuration; they were not evaluated as part of task correctness but are noted under hygiene.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.800); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
